summary.text: 学 is the standardized simplified counterpart of 學, the character used for learning and study. The early construction discussed in the sources belongs to 學 and has competing interpretations; the simplified graph’s present shape does not settle them.

formation.text: 学 is a later, standardized simplified form of 學, so the competing construction accounts concern 學 rather than an independently established ancient construction of 学. The main account describes two hands, 𦥑, manipulating tally-like marks; forms are reported with 五 and 六, or sometimes 爻. Separately, 爻 may have supplied a sound cue in some forms, but this is not established for every form. An alternative proposal reads 爻 with 宀 as crossed roof timbers and a school building. These accounts remain disputed, and the modern shape does not resolve them.

history.text: The selected early-style image is a modern vector tracing identified as an oracle-bone-style form of 學. Its strokes do not decide between the reported interpretations.
學 is the traditional counterpart of standardized simplified 学. The evidence here does not establish the graphic path from early forms to either modern shape.

A later lexicographic account describes 學 as an abbreviated seal-script form of 斆, which it analyzes as 教 and 冖 with 𦥑 supplying the sound. This received account does not confirm the structure of earlier forms.

uncertainties.text: The hands-and-tallies interpretation, a possible sound role for 爻 in some forms, and the alternative 爻-plus-宀 interpretation are distinct competing accounts; none is established for every early form.
The graphic path from early 學 forms to 学 is unresolved. The modern top alone does not establish an ancient roof component or a specific corruption.
An oracle-bone occurrence is reported, but its archaeological date and context are not specified beyond that identification.

senses.text: An oracle-bone occurrence is reported, and learning is identified as an early sense. This is an early documented use, not necessarily the graph’s original meaning.
Bronze-inscription examples are reported for school use; they do not establish when this use first arose relative to learning.
A bronze-inscription example concerns archery instruction. The evidence does not establish a full semantic sequence from learning to teaching.
The phrase 成學 is reported with the meaning “complete one’s studies”; it illustrates a contextual use of 學.

senses.gloss: feel; perceive, written with the graph 學
senses.text: A Han-slip use has 學 writing 覺, “feel” or “perceive.” This is a borrowed spelling for another word, not a development of the learning meaning.

developments.text: Learning and school uses are both reported, but the examples do not show that one developed from the other or establish their relative timing.
Learning and instruction are both documented, but their chronology and any specific semantic transition are not established.

limitations.text: Period-separated examples do not establish a complete chronology or every link among learning, school, instruction, imitation, and knowledge.
The reported Han use of 學 for 覺 has no earlier occurrence or complete sound history documented here.

items.period: Shang period style (oracle-bone script, as identified on file page)
items.tradition: Shang oracle-bone script; modern vector tracing sourced to a Xiaoxuetang glyph record
items.caption: A modern vector tracing identified as a Shang oracle-script form of 學. The broad lower shape and crossing strokes are visible, but do not settle competing interpretations of the early graph.
items.alt: Black glyph on white, with crossing strokes at the top and a broad curved lower form.
items.selection_reason: Offers a visual reference for the reported early form while keeping its construction disputed.

limitations.text: This is a modern tracing, not an excavated inscription. Its appearance cannot resolve whether the early graph depicts hands working with tallies or supports another proposed analysis; the cited oracle-bone occurrence has no narrower date or archaeological context established here.
